brief: BofA's 02 September 2026 volatility weekly carries three arguments. On the US midterms, Kalshi shows a likely Democratic House and a close Senate, yet S&P options price only a 0.82% post-election move and the VIX Sep/Oct/Nov fly sits at 1.11v. BofA reads that as reasonable because midterm one-day S&P moves have averaged 1.3% and beaten the prior month's average in only 33% of cycles since 1975, and because easing equity leverage and low correlation make the election rotation-inducing rather than vol-inducing. So do not overpay for index protection and prefer SPX down-and-out puts, a VIX call spread collar and IWM puts, since regional banks and small caps most underprice 2024 election-week moves. On dividends, SX7E futures trade close to analyst estimates after upgrades, leaving no upside, while SX5E trades below bottom-up estimates for Dec28 and Dec29 and gains AI gearing through ASML's 10% capping, so rotate SX7E divs into SX5E divs or European bank equities. In Korea, vols have roughly halved and the Bubble Risk Indicator has fallen to 0.52 from above 0.8, ending the long-gamma case, and with the KOSPI 200 at 6.2x forward earnings BofA moves to a 110/130 call spread collar funded by an 80% put.
